objective: Building a sustainment plan (processes, metrics, tools) so benefits continue past program completion
secondaryObjectives: Identifying synergies and efficiencies across the program life cycle and updating the benefits realization plan accordingly
Maintaining a benefits register and developing an operations transition plan to guarantee sustainment

sources.cite: PMI, Program Management Professional (PgMP) Examination Content Outline: Strategic Program Alignment 15%, Program Life Cycle Management 44%, Benefits Management 11%, Stakeholder Engagement 16%, Governance 14%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17. The domain weights were confirmed through a summarizing fetch of a training provider's article (eartech.pmtraining.com, 'How to Prepare for the PgMP Certification Exam'), which describes Program Life Cycle Management as 'initiating, planning, executing, controlling, and closing the program across its phases' and Governance as 'the boards, gates, and decision rights that let leadership steer and, when needed, stop a program'. PMI's own outline PDF did not come up in search and PMI's PgMP pages read today do not list the domains; the task wording is the course seed's, to verify against PMI's PDF. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's pgmp-transit-program-steering-review (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the portfolio or program, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are closing a self-service program at Fenmoor Water, a fictional water company: an app, a web portal and a new contact center platform. The program ends in two months; the benefit is a 30% cut in calls.
handover: Operations will own the three products after closure.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a fortnight at a time. A decision comes to you at each board meeting; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Meeting 2: portal users can't pay online and phone in; calls rise 8%.
Meeting 3 (six months on): the unmaintained knowledge base goes stale; calls climb back to 10% below baseline.
Meeting 4: the program runs four more months at 300 thousand dollars a month; calls reach 27%.

synPrompt.title: Duplicated work
synPrompt.context: The app and portal each run a payment module.

choices.label: Consolidate onto one payment module, record the 400 thousand dollar annual saving as an efficiency benefit, and update the benefits realization plan

effects.log: One payment module; the plan is updated.

choices.feedback: Synergies across components are benefits too; the plan records them.

choices.label: Leave both and note it for operations
choices.feedback: The saving is noted but not realized.

choices.label: Delete the portal's payment module to save cost, without migrating users
choices.feedback: Users lose a way to pay; calls go up.

susPrompt.title: After the program ends
susPrompt.context: Nobody will own call deflection or fund the knowledge base.

choices.label: A sustainment plan: operations owns call deflection with a monthly metric, a funded content team for the knowledge base, and the tools handed over
choices.feedback: Benefits continue only if someone owns the processes, metrics and tools after closure.

choices.label: Hand over the documentation
choices.feedback: Documents don't fund or own anything.

choices.label: No plan: the products work
choices.feedback: The knowledge base decays and calls return.

choices.label: Hand over through an operations transition plan with the benefits register, the 26% result against 30%, and the actions operations owns to close the gap

effects.log: Operations takes over with the register.

choices.feedback: Closure verifies transition criteria and hands over the benefits register honestly.

choices.label: Keep the program open indefinitely until 30% is reached
choices.feedback: The program's costs continue for an operational result operations should own.

reflection.question: Write the closure note for the program board: benefits achieved, what keeps them going, and what operations owns.

parts.label: Benefits
parts.criteria: Calls down 26% against 30%; a 400 thousand dollar synergy.
parts.modelAnswer: Calls are down 26% against the 30% target; consolidating payments saves 400 thousand dollars a year.

parts.label: Sustainment and transition
parts.criteria: Operations owns deflection with a metric and funded content team; the register handed over.
parts.modelAnswer: Operations owns call deflection with a monthly metric and a funded content team, and takes the benefits register and the actions to close the gap.

scoring.modelReasoning: Benefits management continues past delivery: synergies between components are captured and recorded in the benefits realization plan; a sustainment plan gives the benefits an owner, metrics, processes, tools and funding after closure; and the transition to operations hands over the benefits register with an honest status.
